@Anna Yeddi I just added this resizer here and wated to double check to see if this HCM styling is ok, or if it needs to have a border styling like the icon buttons?

@Dasha Andriyenko oh, I forgot that we may want to communicate this element is a heading (H1 or H2), to take the guess work away from the engineers. I added an annotation :) Sorry for the extra change

@Dasha Andriyenko I added the text areas here for clarity for engineers how we could accessibly communicate the field's instructions/text.

Idea: "Approaching 700 character limit"

When you hit limit:
"Can't exceed 700 characters"
@Emily Wachowiak I am thinking for this maybe we can have like a bit of a hint. Letting user know how many characters they might have.

@Dasha Andriyenko chatting with @Morgan Rae Reschenberg about it now. This option for the pressed button is the one to go: border is still "Button Text" but the fill and the label are "Selected" pair - this is similar to what we're using for menu items. I'll draft the component in our HCM file for Morgan to review it and will get back with the final version with states :wink:

@Dasha Andriyenko We usually have an offset for the focus outline (attached) - this may be beneficial for WCAG 2.2 Level AA focus compliance (new success criterion). It's not an issue though, commenting in case the focused state got reused from the input field or so. I think the offset comes out of the box too, but again, not an issue, just a note

@Dasha Andriyenko this would be a good example when an icon like "(!)" is beneficial (especially with alt="Error" or "Attention"). Not a blocker and not a bug though

This link needs to be formatted to be location neutral--there should be existing places in the code where eng can grab this. This link is specific to the US

FYI @Dasha Andriyenko confirmed with Jamie re: Reviews: including emoji in the button’s accessible name (i.e. :smile: Good)
1. Great way to have equal experience plus screen readers announce emojis from unicode (same across apps, will be known way). NVDA announces short description of the image and VoiceOver does the long one, but they are the same across platforms, so this is a nice way to do it ;)
@Dasha Andriyenko - l10n review is complete. For SUMO, PM should file a ticket for a new article once we have a release date for the feature
hey! I'll be doing the a11y review, please let me know if you have questions (also, I'm off tomorrow apr 5, so I probably won't start until Monday -- thanks for bearing with me :) )
It would be good to have some sort of signal when users are close or at the limit--like the numbers turn red or something

FYI this is the link but it needs to be formatted so that it renders in the correct language--best to use the same URL format that they use on the current microsurvey https://www.mozilla.org/en-US/about/legal/terms/firefox/
@Emily Wachowiak this is ready for your review

@Anna Yeddi this is just an error mock up of character limit exceeded. My team is still talking about how we can deal with the live character counter display. So for now I mocked this up as a plan B just incase.
@Anna Yeddi please take a look here at all of the HCM breakdown on on the component level.

Instead of character count:
* Use "Bite count"
* % space left
* Warning message
@Dasha Andriyenko We could have autocomplete in here. For users who might be typing out similar issues.

@Dasha Andriyenko 
A11y: it is best to have a character limit to be more transparent. 
* showing live update is better.
* users would still be able to make a prediction if they see letters drop. 
* This can also help users formulate feedback better.

A11y:
Pressed state should have a slight border to indicate "pressed/ persistent state.
@Dasha Andriyenko here's the content I recommend for the next round of testing...lmk what you think!
Is there an option if the user doesn't want to tell us more? Like, can they just submit without checking a box?
I think Submit works, but "Send" or "Send feedback" might be less formal @Emily Wachowiak

OPO: "How is the translation" felt a bit stiff perhaps? Also had this inclination to get more specific... Alt takes: 

"How's the translation?"
"How's the translation quality"?
Just an OPO but I like Just OK a bit more than OK

The 'is' does throw me a bit. Just riffin...

How was the translation?
How was the translation quality?
How'd we do with the translation?

can this options split based on the selection?

alt: what could we improve?
jeff: what could be better?
It would be harder to estimate number of characters left. Easier to say "this is too long" instead of how many characters left.

For legal review:
* need to confirm if this is anonymous.
think about colour contrast
How is the translation
@Dasha Andriyenko double check best practice with UR on this.

Acorn: 
* Looks like Microsurvey is a unique component that wasn't run by acorn. So it's not 100% the same as some of our other panels. Should we try to stick to our panel design, or should we align closer to the panel. Make our pop ups look and feel the same 
* Panel with x in the corner in our panel? Potentially a cancel button instead. 
* The padding is also bigger then our pannels

Initial copy ideas:
What was wrong with this translation?
* Wrong meaning
* Awkward or incoherent language
* Wrong translation of symbols or numbers
* Wrong source language detected
* Other
